does: Dries and browns bread, nuts or spices in dry heat, which makes them crisp and wakes their scent.
how: Spread the food in a single layer on a tray or in a dry pan.
Use a moderate heat: an oven, a grill or a pan with no fat.
Turn bread once. Shake nuts and spices often.
Tip nuts and spices out of the hot pan as soon as they are done, as they go on browning in it.

cues.text: Bread is dry and pale gold. Nuts are a shade darker than they were.
A warm, nutty scent rises. An acrid smell means it has gone too far.

mistakes.mistake: Walking away, as nuts go from golden to burnt within moments.
mistakes.fix: Stay with them and shake the pan.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving toasted nuts or spices in the hot pan, where they keep browning.
mistakes.fix: Tip them onto a cold plate at once.
